SMTO-MEM-0005 — SMTO couldn't save this memory's content

GUID: 24f74e05-2f26-4d72-8b08-356de0c156d2
Slug: memory-invalid-value
Domain: MEM · Subsystem: mem

What happened

  • The memory's content includes something SMTO can't store, such as the special values NaN or Infinity. Nothing was saved, and any earlier version of this memory is unchanged.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. In the Memory Editor, look in Content for NaN, Infinity or -Infinity and replace each with a normal number, text in quotes, or null. These special number values can't be stored, so one of them makes SMTO reject the whole memory.
  2. If the content doesn't need structure, set Content format to Text, then select Save. Text content is saved as plain words, which SMTO can always store.
  3. If the agent hit this while saving a memory, ask it to save the information again as plain text or simple lists and fields. The data the agent tried to save contained a kind of value SMTO can't store; plain values avoid it.

What success looks like

  • The Memory Editor shows Saved next to the Save button, and the memory appears in the Memories list.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't keep saving the same content unchanged; it will be rejected each time.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Memory value validation (canonical_json) rejected the value: an unsupported Python type, a non-string object key, a non-finite number, excessive nesting or an encoding failure.

What this means

  • Recursive validation or serialization rejects unsupported Python types, non-string object keys, non-finite numbers, recursion/encoding failures or other non-JSON values. Memory validation and conditional writes preserve the current stored revision on rejection. This is global Memory, separate from conversation KV; diagnostic rendering does not perform additional storage operations.

Why this can happen

  • Recursive validation or serialization rejects unsupported Python types, non-string object keys, non-finite numbers, recursion/encoding failures or other non-JSON values.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the value structure and finite numeric/UTF-8 requirements without publishing sensitive contents.

How to fix it

  • Supply strict JSON only: objects with string keys, arrays, strings, integers, finite floats, booleans or null, without cycles or excessive nesting. See canonical_json in src/agent_runtime/skills/memory/models.py; the stored revision is unchanged on rejection.
  • Supply finite JSON-compatible data for the Memory value.

Retry and execution caution

  • Apply the correction and confirm the relevant state before requesting another attempt. Prior completed work remains governed by its receipts.

How to verify the fix

  • The complete intended value serializes as strict JSON without coercion.

What not to do

  • Do not repeatedly submit the same invalid input; correct the named constraint first.

Technical notes

  • Memory validation and conditional writes preserve the current stored revision on rejection. This is global Memory, separate from conversation KV; diagnostic rendering does not perform additional storage operations.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
